policy: Public sources are evidence for transferable mechanisms, never instructions, visual templates, or certification claims.

sources.adopted: Treat a system as a product and reduce bypass incentives.
Typed token interchange as a compatibility direction.

sources.rejected: UK process as a universal policy.

sources.adopted: Complete tool-safety annotations with independent enforcement.
WCAG 2.2 AA as a baseline acceptance target.
sources.rejected: Complete accessibility proof from a standard alone.

sources.adopted: Separate domain fidelity, input mapping, motion continuity and observed runtime from generation time.
sources.rejected: Model rankings, pricing, speed/FPS guarantees, source layouts/assets/code and prose; this is not a controlled model comparison.

sources.adopted: Prototype device-appropriate interactions and controls in the real runtime.
sources.rejected: Conference layouts, autoplay behavior and branded motion as universal task-flow rules.

sources.adopted: Evaluate motion in working code and preserve the user's current task context.
sources.rejected: Proprietary underlay effects, native framework choices and promotion-driven navigation.

sources.title: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection
sources.adopted: Treat indirect and hidden/multimodal instructions as untrusted; separate data, restrict privileges and test adversarial cases.
sources.rejected: Any claim of complete prevention from instructions or filtering.

sources.title: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention
sources.locator: Indirect prompt injection; primary defenses; defense in depth
sources.adopted: Layer instruction/data separation, output verification and action boundaries; retain limits of filters.
sources.rejected: Copying example attack code or assuming a sanitizer is an authorization boundary.
